_about: A real, finished example (University of Bath, trimmed to one course and one programme) showing how each field is filled. Copy the shape, not the facts.

example.name: University of Bath

settingEvidence.evidence: We are a campus university in the South West of England and offer courses in engineering, humanities, management, science and social science.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for Home (UK) students on standard full-time courses starting in 2027 (2027/28). Bath says the 2027/28 regulated fee is still to be confirmed by the UK government (subject to parliamentary approval); placement/study-abroad year fees are reduced.

source.evidence: Home UK tuition fees are £10,050 for standard full-time courses in 2027/28.

livingCosts.text: University self-catered (non-catered) halls cost about £98–£315 a week including bills, average £183 a week (2026/27). Bath's sample student budget for a 38-week year totals about £12,392.

source.evidence: *University Non-Catered Accommodation (ranges from £98-£315 per week) Average cost £183 p/w. inclusive of bills

openDays.text: Next in-person undergraduate open days are in June 2027 (exact dates not announced yet).

source.evidence: Our next in-person Open Days are in June 2027.

contextual.summary: Home-fee applicants who meet any one of Bath's contextual criteria automatically get a lower contextual offer and extra consideration from an Admissions Progression Team.
contextual.typicalReduction: Two grades lower than the typical entry requirements for most courses (Economics & Mathematics: one grade lower for 2026 and 2027 entry).

criteria.detail: Recorded as eligible for Free School Meals in the National Pupil Database (England, or equivalent in NI/Wales) at any point during Key Stage 3 or Key Stage 4. FSM during sixth form does not count.

Home postcode when you apply is in an area of high socio-economic disadvantage (IMD quintiles 1 or 2) and you attended a UK state school or college for at least two full academic years in your last four years.
Care leaver or care experienced, aged 25 or under when you start, with evidence.
Young carer, aged 25 or under when you start, with evidence.
Estranged student, aged 25 or under when you start, with evidence.
You hold leave in the UK as a refugee, asylum seeker or person with humanitarian protection, or you are the child of someone who does.

contextual.rulesText: You will be considered for contextual admissions (including contextual offers) if you are eligible for UK fees and meet any one of the criteria. Contextual offers are automatic and replace the typical or alternative offers; contextual and alternative offers do not stack.

source.evidence: You will be considered for contextual admissions (including contextual offers) if you are a student eligible for UK fees and you meet any one of the following criteria:

programmes.name: Discover Bath
programmes.summary: Free 2-night residential summer school for Year 12 students from widening participation backgrounds, with subject streams including Economics and Accounting/Business.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 (or equivalent) students who are academically able to study their chosen subject at Bath and meet Bath's widening participation criteria. You can only do one of Pathway to Bath, Bath Ambitions or Discover Bath.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Meet one or more WP criteria: eligible for FSM between ages 11 and 16; home postcode in IMD quintiles 1-2 (deciles 1-4) and no more than two years at an independent/international school in your last four years; care leaver; young carer; refugee, asylum seeker or humanitarian protection; irreconcilably estranged from parents.
benefits: Free on-campus accommodation, meals and academic sessions; reasonable UK travel reimbursed
Possible guaranteed conditional offer from Bath if you complete the programme and meet the criteria (terms currently published for 2026 and 2027 entry)
UCAS, personal statement and student finance support
programmes.subjects: Social Sciences stream (incl. Economics, Politics, Psychology, Sociology) or Accounting, Management and Business stream (Business and Marketing, Accounting and Finance)

runs.text: Social Sciences and Accounting/Management/Business streams: Wednesday 4 – Friday 6 August 2027 (2 nights)

programmes.infoNote: 2027 dates published; application deadline not yet published.
notConfirmed: Guaranteed-offer terms are only published for 2026 and 2027 entry, not 2028 entry

courses.name: Economics
courses.lengthNote: Also offered as a 4-year course with a professional placement or study abroad in Year 3 (course code D101)

offer.text: A*AA in three A levels including Mathematics

source.evidence: A*AA in three A levels including Mathematics.

subjectRequirements.note: A level Mathematics required; typical offer A*AA including Mathematics (the page does not say the A* must be in Mathematics). Contextual and alternative offers ask for A in Mathematics.

preferredSubjects.note: The strongest applicants take A level Mathematics plus two of these preferred subjects (Geography and Psychology are both on the list). Subjects studied are weighted 20% in selection.

gcse.subject: English
gcse.note: GCSE English Language or Literature grade 4/C. Wider GCSE profile weighted 50% in selection (best eight grades incl. Maths and English); strongest applicants have had mostly 9/A* grades.

courses.gcseText: GCSE English Language or Literature grade 4 or C (or equivalent from English language category B). Your wider GCSE profile is also a significant factor in how we select students for offer for this course.

subjectsEvidence.evidence: A level Mathematics is required for this course. You do not need to have previously studied Economics or Politics.

admissionsTest.effect: No admissions test. Bath stopped considering TMUA and MAT scores from 2025 entry; maths tests are only used for some Mathematics degrees.

source.evidence: For 2025 onwards we will no longer be considering TMUA or MAT scores in our admissions.

alternativeOffers.conditions: AAB including A in Mathematics, automatically if you meet Bath's contextual criteria (replaces the typical and alternative offers).

source.evidence: AAB in three A levels including A in Mathematics.

alternativeOffers.conditions: AAA or A*AB including A in Mathematics, plus grade A in an EPQ or IEPQ (or an appropriate grade in another recognised project qualification). Not available if you get the contextual offer.

source.evidence: AAA or A*AB in three A levels including A in Mathematics plus one of:

alternativeOffers.conditions: AAA or A*AB including A in Mathematics, plus grade A in AS level Further Mathematics (if not taking the full A level), or grade B in a fourth A level where your four A levels include A level Further Mathematics.

source.evidence: grade A in AS level Further Mathematics (except if you are studying an A level in that subject)

alternativeOffers.conditions: Guaranteed conditional offer if you successfully complete Pathway to Bath, Discover Bath or Bath Ambitions, apply by the UCAS on-time deadline, are predicted no more than two grades below the typical offer and meet the course's minimum requirements. Terms are published for 2026 and 2027 entry only; the offer grades are not stated.
alternativeOffers.programme: Pathway to Bath / Discover Bath / Bath Ambitions

source.evidence: We will therefore guarantee an offer to those who successfully complete the programme (Pathway, Discover or Bath Ambitions, formerly Target Bath) and meet our eligibility criteria as outlined below.

courses.notes: Selection weighting (A level applicants): GCSE profile 50%, predicted grades 20% (Maths grade particularly important), subjects 20%, personal statement 10%. Economics, Economics with Politics and their placement/abroad versions are assessed together; no benefit in applying to more than one. Most offers are made in February and March.

notes: No 2028-entry course pages yet (checked 2026-10-17: bath.ac.uk/courses/undergraduate-2028/ returns 404), so all courses use 2027 entry.
